control 'safbox-firstboot-3' do
  impact 1.0
  title 'The first-boot unit is not in an ordering cycle with multi-user.target'
  desc 'The unit is wanted by multi-user.target, so it is ordered before it. If it is ordered after a ' \
       'unit that itself comes after multi-user.target (cloud-final.service, cloud-init.target), ' \
       'systemd breaks the cycle by deleting the first-boot job and first boot never runs.'

  unit = 'safbox-firstboot.service'
  after = command("systemctl show -p After --value #{unit}").stdout.split
  after.each do |dependency|
    describe "#{unit} ordered after #{dependency}, which" do
      subject { command("systemctl show -p After --value #{dependency}").stdout.split }
      it { should_not include 'multi-user.target' }
    end
  end

  describe command('journalctl -b --no-pager -o cat -u safbox-firstboot.service') do
    its('stdout') { should_not match(/ordering cycle/i) }
  end
end

  desc 'With guest-exec or guest-file-* enabled, anyone with administrative access to the hypervisor can run commands and read or write files inside the appliance without logging in. The distribution ships a filter that disables them; the image must keep it unmodified.'

    subject { mode }
    it { should be_in %w[allow block] }

  bindings = command("podman pod inspect heimdall --format '{{json .InfraConfig.PortBindings}}'").stdout
  describe 'Ports the heimdall pod publishes on the host' do
    subject { (JSON.parse(bindings.empty? ? '{}' : bindings) || {}).transform_values { |b| b.map { |x| "#{x['HostIp']}:#{x['HostPort']}" } } }
    it { should eq('3000/tcp' => ["127.0.0.1:#{loopback_port}"]) }

    its('stdout') { should eq '200' }
  end

  describe command(%q(podman exec heimdall node -p "require('crypto').getFips()")) do
    its('stdout.strip') { should eq '1' }
  end

  impact 1.0
  title 'The distribution and microarchitecture level of the running image are recorded'
  desc 'ADR-0001 Risks: validation records which distribution and microarchitecture level an image was built from so a lab artifact is never mistaken for a release artifact. The values appear in the test descriptions of this control: the package architecture is what the image was built from (x86_64_v2 on the AlmaLinux v2 media), the loader level is what this CPU supports.'

    it { should_not be_nil }
  end

  package_arch = command("rpm -q --qf '%{ARCH}' glibc").stdout.strip
  describe "image package architecture #{package_arch}" do
    subject { package_arch }
    it { should match(/^(x86_64(_v[234])?|aarch64)$/) }

  loader = command('/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 --help')
  if loader.exit_status.zero?
    level = loader.stdout[/x86-64-v\d+(?= \(supported)/] || 'none'
    describe "highest microarchitecture level this CPU supports #{level}" do
      subject { level }
      it { should match(/^x86-64-v[234]$/) }
    end
  else
    describe "microarchitecture level not applicable on #{os.arch}" do
      subject { os.arch }
      it { should_not eq 'x86_64' }
    end
  end
end

control 'safbox-tools-2' do

  title 'The SAF CLI is installed at its pinned version on the distribution Node.js'
  desc 'ADR-0001 Phase 3: the MITRE SAF CLI (tools group safbox-tools-2), installed from npm at ' \

  only_if('the SAF CLI is not in expected_tools (tools group safbox-tools-2 switched off)') do
    tool_expected.call('saf-cli')
  end

  version = input('saf_cli_version')
  # Run in a scratch directory that is removed afterwards: the SAF CLI
  # writes saf-cli.log to its working directory and has no option to stop it.
  # One sh -c, because sudo (the profile's --sudo) applies to the first word
  # of a command line only.
  saf_version = %q(sh -c 'd=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$d" && /usr/local/bin/saf --version; rc=$?; cd / && rm -rf "$d"; exit $rc')
  describe command(saf_version) do
    its('exit_status') { should eq 0 }
    its('stdout') { should match(%r{^@mitre/saf/#{Regexp.escape(version)} }) }

  # The SAF CLI writes saf-cli.log to its working directory on every run,
  # even for --version. Running it must leave nothing in the scanning
  # user's home or in /, so a scan of a consumer's box leaves no residue.
  scan_user = command('printf %s "${SUDO_USER:-$(id -un)}"').stdout.strip
  scan_home = command("getent passwd #{scan_user} | cut -d: -f6").stdout.strip
  ["#{scan_home}/saf-cli.log", '/saf-cli.log'].uniq.each do |residue|
    describe file(residue) do
      it { should_not exist }
    end
  end

  if input('fips_required')
    describe command("node -p \"require('crypto').getFips()\"") do
      its('exit_status') { should eq 0 }

    end

control 'safbox-guest-agent-1' do
  impact 1.0
  title "The guest agent keeps the distribution's RPC filter: no in-guest exec or file access"
  desc 'With guest-exec or guest-file-* enabled, anyone with administrative access to the hypervisor can run commands and read or write files inside the appliance without logging in. The distribution ships a filter that disables them; the image must keep it unmodified.'
  # On platforms without a guest-agent channel the agent cannot run; the
  # deploy sets guest_agent_expected=false there. Everywhere else a stopped
  # agent is a failure, not a skip.
  only_if('guest agent not expected on this platform (guest_agent_expected=false)') do
    input('guest_agent_expected')
  end

  describe 'qemu-guest-agent main process' do
    subject { main_pid }
    it { should match(/^[1-9]\d*$/) }
  end

  mode, rpcs = rpc_filter.call(agent_args)
  denied = input('guest_agent_denied_rpcs')

  describe 'guest agent RPC filter mode' do
    subject { mode }
    it { should be_in %w[allow block] }
  end

  if mode == 'allow'
    describe 'RPCs the guest agent allows' do
      subject { rpcs }
      denied.each { |rpc| it { should_not include rpc } }
    end
  elsif mode == 'block'
    describe 'RPCs the guest agent blocks' do
      subject { rpcs }
      denied.each { |rpc| it { should include rpc } }
    end
  end

  describe command("systemctl show -p DropInPaths --value #{unit}") do
    its('stdout.strip') { should be_empty }
  end

  describe command('rpm -V --nomtime qemu-guest-agent') do
    its('stdout') { should be_empty }
  end
end

  desc 'ADR-0001 Phase 3: the MITRE SAF CLI (tools group safbox-tools-2), installed from npm at ' \
       "its pinned version and run by the distribution's Node.js, which uses the system OpenSSL and so its FIPS provider."
  only_if('the SAF CLI is not in expected_tools (tools group safbox-tools-2 switched off)') do
    tool_expected.call('saf-cli')
  end

  version = input('saf_cli_version')
  # Run in a scratch directory that is removed afterwards: the SAF CLI
  # writes saf-cli.log to its working directory and has no option to stop it.
  # One sh -c, because sudo (the profile's --sudo) applies to the first word
  # of a command line only.
  saf_version = %q(sh -c 'd=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$d" && /usr/local/bin/saf --version; rc=$?; cd / && rm -rf "$d"; exit $rc')
  describe command(saf_version) do
    its('exit_status') { should eq 0 }
    its('stdout') { should match(%r{^@mitre/saf/#{Regexp.escape(version)} }) }
  end

  instance_exec('SAF CLI', version, &status_row)

  # The SAF CLI writes saf-cli.log to its working directory on every run,
  # even for --version. Running it must leave nothing in the scanning
  # user's home or in /, so a scan of a consumer's box leaves no residue.
  scan_user = command('printf %s "${SUDO_USER:-$(id -un)}"').stdout.strip
  scan_home = command("getent passwd #{scan_user} | cut -d: -f6").stdout.strip
  ["#{scan_home}/saf-cli.log", '/saf-cli.log'].uniq.each do |residue|
    describe file(residue) do
      it { should_not exist }
    end
  end

  if input('fips_required')
    describe command("node -p \"require('crypto').getFips()\"") do
      its('exit_status') { should eq 0 }

  title 'Vulcan runs, reachable only on the loopback address, with FIPS-mode crypto'
  desc "ADR-0001 Quality Standards (security by design): services bind to the proxy, not to all interfaces. The pod publishes Vulcan's port on 127.0.0.1 only, for the TLS proxy; PostgreSQL is published nowhere. Vulcan's Ruby links the image's OpenSSL (Red Hat UBI 9), which runs its FIPS provider under the host's FIPS enforcement."
  only_if('Vulcan is not in expected_services, or this is not a deployed clone') do
    service_expected.call('vulcan') && input('firstboot_completed_expected')
  end

  %w[vulcan-pod vulcan-db vulcan].each do |unit|
    describe command("systemctl is-active #{unit}.service") do
      its('stdout.strip') { should eq 'active' }
    end
  end

  bindings = command("podman pod inspect vulcan --format '{{json .InfraConfig.PortBindings}}'").stdout
  describe 'Ports the vulcan pod publishes on the host' do
    subject { (JSON.parse(bindings.empty? ? '{}' : bindings) || {}).transform_values { |b| b.map { |x| "#{x['HostIp']}:#{x['HostPort']}" } } }
    it { should eq('3000/tcp' => ["127.0.0.1:#{loopback_port}"]) }
  end

  [loopback_port, 5432].each do |p|
    describe port(p) do
      its('addresses') { should_not include '0.0.0.0' }
      its('addresses') { should_not include '::' }
    end
  end

  # RAILS_FORCE_SSL redirects plain HTTP; the proxy says the client used HTTPS.
  describe command("curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'X-Forwarded-Proto: https' http://127.0.0.1:#{loopback_port}/up") do
    its('stdout') { should eq '200' }
  end

  describe command(%q(podman exec vulcan ruby -ropenssl -e 'print OpenSSL.fips_mode')) do
    its('stdout.strip') { should eq 'true' }
  end

  describe command('runuser -u nobody -- /usr/local/bin/safbox status') do
    its('stdout') { should match(/^Vulcan:\s+active$/) }

profiles.summary: Asserts that a SAFBox image or clone on the RHEL 10 family carries the appliance foundation (ADR-0001 Phases 2 and 3): FIPS mode, Secure Boot, the expected OS, enabled units, the guest agent's RPC filter, podman and Quadlet, the safbox CLI, the first-boot framework, the pinned tools (CINC Auditor, SAF CLI, Ansible and the Lockdown collections, Packer), no distribution default user and, once sealed, the build record and the absence of build residue; and the services (Phases 5 and 6, and the TLS proxy): Heimdall and Vulcan as Quadlet pods on the loopback address with secrets from first boot, behind an nginx TLS proxy with a first-boot certificate. Every control is impact 1.0, so the thresholds in verify/thresholds/ can name each one in the critical bucket, which no STIG control uses, except documented findings: known weaknesses kept visible as low-impact controls that fail, tagged finding. Runs alone or through the verify/inspec-safbox wrapper, from the build runner over SSH; the sealed template's own invariants are asserted by the seal step itself.
